title: Console: add control plane read APIs for Dedicated burst usage/limits/denials
author: Chloe Martin
release_notes: Expose read-only burst endpoints for Console (usage series, effective limits, denial reason breakdown).
Adds RBAC scopes and internal-only routing for Console callers; no data plane behavior changes.
description:
Summary: Console needs a reliable, supportable way to display (1) current/effective burst configuration (enabled, caps, cooldown), (2) customer-facing burst usage over time (GPU-seconds + request-level counters), and (3) denial breakdowns by standardized reason code (from pr-23795) with enough detail to debug without exposing sensitive fleet internals. This PR adds a small set of read-only Control Plane endpoints and backing query plumbing (metering + admission controller aggregates) to power the new Dedicated Burst pages in Console (DES-219 / ENG-4855).

Context / Motivation: During beta onboarding we’ve been hand-walking customers through Grafana + internal tools to answer basic questions like “how close are we to our burst cap?”, “why did we get a spike in denials?”, and “did we hit a cooldown or a fleet safety gate?”. Support also needs a consistent surface to reference in tickets (e.g. SUP-28503 / SUP-28411) without having to grant wide dashboard access. These endpoints are intentionally read-only and are scoped to a tenant + region/hardware class view that matches what we promise in the product.

What’s included (API): Adds GET endpoints under the internal Control Plane API (Console-facing) with stable response contracts and pagination/limits:
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/status?region=us-east&hardware_class=h100
  - Returns: burst_enabled (bool), priority_tier, effective_baseline_gpus, max_burst_gpus, max_burst_ratio, per_window_burst_gpu_seconds_cap, cooldown_seconds, current_cooldown_state, updated_at, updated_by (redacted actor), and a small set of computed fields (effective_max_throughput_hint, is_fleet_circuit_breaker_active).
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/usage?start=...&end=...&step=60s&region=...&hardware_class=...
  - Returns time series: burst_gpu_seconds, burst_requests_admitted, burst_requests_denied, burst_requests_queued (if enabled in config), plus an optional top-level summary (max/avg) for the window.
  - Enforces max range (7d) and min step (60s) to control cost/cardinality.
- GET /v1/console/tenants/{tenant_id}/burst/denials?start=...&end=...&region=...&hardware_class=...
  - Returns breakdown by denial_reason_code (e.g. CAP_REACHED, COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, POOL_SATURATED, FLEET_SAFETY_CAP, TELEMETRY_STALE, POLICY_DISABLED, RATE_LIMITED) and counts, plus an optional “most_recent_denial_at”.

Key implementation details:
- Data sources:
  - Usage series comes from the metering aggregation tables (same pipeline used for billing exports) but explicitly filtered to “burst portion” (above baseline allocation). This uses the idempotency fixes from pr-24108 to avoid double-counting retries.
  - Denial breakdown comes from admission controller decision logs aggregated into a small rollup table (1m buckets). We intentionally do not return raw decision logs to Console.
  - Effective limits are computed by composing tenant config (control plane tenant model), region/hardware rollout gates (feature flags), and global circuit breaker state (pr-23919).
- Caching:
  - Adds 30s server-side cache for status endpoint; usage/denials are uncached but benefit from rollups.
  - Adds ETag support on /status to reduce Console polling cost.
- Auth/RBAC:
  - New permissions: tenant.burst.read and tenant.burst.console_read.
  - Console service uses service-to-service auth with mTLS + JWT claims; endpoint enforces “Console caller only” gate and tenant scoping.
  - Response field updated_by is returned as one of: "customer", "redwood_admin", or "automation" (no raw email), matching Security guidance.
- Error handling contract:
  - 400 for invalid ranges/step; 404 for unknown tenant; 409 when bursting is not rolled out in region/hardware (Console can show “not available”); 503 when upstream rollup store is unavailable (Console should degrade gracefully).
  - Uses standardized error codes in body for Console to map to UX states; does not leak internal pool IDs.

Files/areas changed (high level):
- control-plane/api/console/burst_endpoints.go (new handlers)
- control-plane/service/burst_read_service.go (compose effective limits + query rollups)
- control-plane/auth/scopes.go (new scopes)
- metering/rollups/burst_usage_rollup.sql (new view + retention notes)
- admission-controller/rollups/denial_reason_rollup.sql (new rollup job)
- proto/controlplane/console_burst.proto (response contracts)
- docs/internal/console-burst-api.md (internal consumer doc + examples)

Example (curl): GET /v1/console/tenants/tnt_8f3.../burst/denials?start=2025-04-30T00:00:00Z&end=2025-04-30T06:00:00Z&region=us-east&hardware_class=h100 -> {"window":"2025-04-30T00:00:00Z/2025-04-30T06:00:00Z","denials":[{"reason_code":"CAP_REACHED","count":1842},{"reason_code":"COOLDOWN_ACTIVE","count":311},{"reason_code":"POOL_SATURATED","count":97}]}

Tests:
- Unit tests for range validation, RBAC enforcement, and effective limit composition.
- Integration tests with seeded rollup data (golden fixtures) verifying stable output ordering and reason code mapping.
- Added a small load test for /usage (step=60s, 7d max) to ensure query time stays < 500ms P95 on staging.

Operational notes:
- Retention for the rollup tables is 30 days (Console uses 24h/7d defaults). Long-term reporting remains via scheduled exports (pr-24091).
- Added dashboards for endpoint error rates and latency under the existing Console API folder; alerts are non-paging (warning) unless sustained 5xx > 2%.

Review/Discussion highlights:
- Dylan: requested ETag + cache on /status to avoid tight polling; added.
- Ethan: asked to ensure determinism between “effective limits” in status and enforcement; status now reads the same compiled policy bundle used by the admission controller (same revision hash returned in response).
- Allison: called out label cardinality risks for denials; we only aggregate by reason_code (bounded set) and do not expose per-route labels.
- Sean: asked for explicit behavior when rollout gate blocks region/hardware; added 409 BURST_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION and documented Console fallback UX.

CI:
- build-and-unit-tests: pass
- lint (go + buf): pass
- db-migrations-check: pass
- integration-tests-control-plane: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main. Follow-ups: (1) Console wiring PR to switch from Grafana links to these endpoints (owned by Console team, tracked in ENG-4855), (2) add “denial sample traces” for internal-only support tooling (separate PR; keep Console surface aggregated).
